results.title: Kremlin declines comment on reports 700,000 Russian soldiers killed in Ukraine war
results.content: Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov on Wednesday declined to comment on reports in Russian and international news outlets that around 700,000 Russian soldiers have been killed in the Ukraine war so far. The reports were based on hacked data from Russia's official statistics agency. Peskov said only the defence ministry can disclose figures and told reporters "not to pay attention to any other data".

results.title: French Mayors Conference: 2027 Elysée hopeful Lisnard reelected association president
results.content: The Mayor of Cannes, David Lisnard, has been re-elected president of the Association of Mayors of France, securing a comfortable victory in a vote announced on Wednesday. Lisnard is also a candidate in next year's French presidential election. For more on what his re-election could mean, FRANCE 24's James André reports from the Association of Mayors' convention in Paris.

results.title: Houthi rebels close in on Aden, Yemeni forces dig in behind fortified line
results.content: Iran-backed Houthi rebels have advanced to within about 60 kilometers of the seat of Yemen’s internationally recognized government in the southern city of Aden, but the forces fighting them have set up a fortified line to defend the city, a military official said Tuesday. The Houthis' advance toward Aden has come after forces allied with the government withdrew from areas on the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, allowing the Houthis to consolidate their grip on territory around the crucial waterway.

results.title: Moldova issues emergency kit guide, prepares citizens for possible expansion of Ukraine war
results.content: As the war in Ukraine has highlighted the importance of civilian preparedness, Moldova has launched its own emergency readiness programme. Medicine, batteries and three days' worth of food are among the essentials citizens are encouraged to keep at hand, in case they need to leave at a moment's notice.

results.title: Exiled Catalan separatist Puigdemont to return to Spain after election
results.content: Catalan separatist ​and former regional leader Carles Puigdemont said on Wednesday he would end nearly a decade of self-imposed exile in Belgium and return to Spain on December 12, ​after ‌this weekend's national election. Puigdemont, whose legal troubles in ⁠Spain are over after the Supreme Court earlier this week applied an amnesty law to shelve the ‌criminal case against him, said at a televised news conference from ⁠Brussels that he would unveil his proposal for a renewed Catalan independence push on December 17. FRANCE 24's Sarah Morris reports from Madrid, Spain.

results.title: 'Paper Tiger': Scarlett Johansson and Adam Driver shine in Russian mob thriller
results.content: This week on arts24, Emma Jones and Dheepthika Laurent discuss the latest film releases. We start with "Paper Tiger", a Russian mob thriller starring Adam Driver, Scarlett Johansson and Miles Teller. It is a return to familiar crime thriller territory for James Gray, the director behind "Little Odessa" and "The Yards".

results.title: Trump announces new tariffs on EU, China despite US midterms defeat
results.content: President Donald Trump's administration on Wednesday reignited global trade tensions by proposing new tariffs on some of the largest US trading partners, including the EU, Japan and Taiwan. China could be slapped with a 20 percent tariff, a senior official said. The announcement came weeks after a cost-of-living crisis landed the Republicans a sweeping defeat in the US midterms.

results.title: California braces for flooding threat from huge tides, El Nino
results.content: Californians are preparing for a confluence of exceptionally high tides and El Nino-fueled weather that threatens coastal areas with extreme flooding during the busiest US travel week of the year. The San Francisco Bay Area is expected to get hit hard with a one-two punch of inclement weather and monster tides, which forecasters warned could push seawater into low-lying areas on Wednesday and Thursday.

results.title: 'Historic' space mission: China launches Shenzhou 24 spacecraft carrying Pakistani astronaut
results.content: China on Wednesday launched the Shenzhou 24 spacecraft with three astronauts — two Chinese and a Pakistani — sending the first foreign crew member to its space station. It successfully separated from a rocket and entered its predetermined orbit. The launch marked the first joint flight involving Chinese and foreign astronauts in the history of China’s crewed space program.

results.title: Colombian authorities rescue all hostages held at Cartagena supermarket
results.content: Security forces rescued all the hostages held for nearly a day at a supermarket in the northern Colombian tourist city of Cartagena, President Abelardo de la Espriella said early Wednesday. The president said that the men were “common criminals” who fled into the supermarket after a failed attempt to hold up an armored truck. The hostage situation broke out as Colombia is experiencing a wave of attacks by rebel groups on government targets.

results.title: Violence against women in the digital age: When the internet becomes a weapon
results.content: November 25th is the United Nation's International Day for the Elimination of Violence Against Women. In the age of social media and artificial intelligence, there are now new spaces in which violence against women has appeared, with the internet now a growing weapon in the hands of abusers. 85% of women who spend time online have witnessed violence, and 38% have been the target of it.

results.title: US army to detonate stockpile of unstable bomb-making chemicals in Iowa
results.content: The US military will on Wednesday detonate some 10,000 pounds of unstable and degraded explosive material in Iowa, where local residents were urged to evacuate amid concerns over possible toxic lead contamination. US officials say the 68 drums of lead azide are at risk of spontaneous explosion. A series of safety measures are being taken to curb potential contamination from the blast, but the Army has encouraged residents of a small town and other nearby areas to leave "out of an abundance of caution."

results.title: The forgotten victims of femicide: Children orphaned by violence in Italy
results.content: November 25th is International Day for the Elimination of Violence Against Women. The forgotten victims of femicide are the children who find themselves motherless, often because their mother was killed by their own father. Italy recorded 97 female homicides in 2025 – 62 of them were committed by a partner. These crimes leave whole families devastated and children who have to grow up without their parents. FRANCE 24’s correspondent in Italy, Natalia Mendoza, reports.

results.title: Israeli MPs advance bill for inquiry into security failings that led to October 7 Hamas attack
results.content: Israeli MPs on Wednesday gave their initial approval for the creation of a commission to investigate the security failures that led to the October 7, 2023 attack by Hamas. Caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who was in power when the attack happened, has repeatedly rejected calls to set up such a probe.

results.title: Producer and guitarist Ginton on jazz, remixing big hits and collaborating on a track for Drake
results.content: Amsterdam-based guitarist, DJ and music producer Ginton is known for blending reggae, Afro, Caribbean and electronic music. He told FRANCE 24 that his background in jazz was "the reason I can make the music I make today". He also told us of his "surprise" in collaborating on a track for Drake's album "Honestly, Nevermind". He spoke to us in Perspective.

results.title: ‘A symbol of hope’: Pakistan celebrates as astronaut enters orbit
results.content: Muhammad Zeeshan Ali has become the first Pakistani to reach orbit after blasting off on board a Chinese mission to the country’s Tiangong space station on Tuesday. The Pakistan Air Force pilot and payload specialist’s feat was celebrated by cheers and rapturous applause by those watching in his homeland.

results.title: Violence against women: Its many forms and the paths to justice
results.content: PRESS REVIEW – Wednesday, November 25: Some 21 percent of women say they have suffered "economic violence", while others are exploring new types of justice for their abusers. In other news, recent leaks on Russian troop losses show 349 deaths in Mali, Russia's biggest military deployment in Africa. As Spain prepares to head to the polls, Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez announces a raft of social measures. Finally, a plucky young cat from Essex has taken a train to London.

results.title: Yemen's Houthis claim attacks on Riyadh financial district, Saudi refinery
results.content: Yemen's Houthis on Wednesday claimed attacks targeting the financial district in the Saudi capital and the sprawling Ras Tanura refinery in the kingdom's oil-rich east, in retaliation for strikes on their territory. Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree described the attack targeting the refinery as "accurate and direct", saying it "caused fires to break out at the facility". He said the attack on Riyadh was "carried out in three phases, with strikes hitting their targets accurately".

results.title: Cyberattack exposes unclassified information from CIA system, US media reports
results.content: A recently discovered hack on a CIA analysis system exposed some unclassified information, US media reported on Tuesday. The breach is the latest in a series of cyber attacks that have targeted US government departments and major companies in recent weeks.

results.title: 🔴 Surprise Eurostar strike cancels London, Paris and Brussels trains
Surprise Eurostar strike cancels London, Paris and Brussels trains
results.content: Several Eurostar trains connecting London, Paris and Brussels were cancelled in a surprise strike on Wednesday. The train operator did not specify who exactly was striking or the reasons why.

results.title: 🔴 Colombia president says all hostages freed, one assailant killed after supermarket hostage siege
AFCON 2025: CAS gives title back to Senegal as Morocco vows to challenge verdict
results.content: The Court of Arbitration for Sport has handed down its ruling: Senegal is officially the 2025 AFCON champion. The Moroccan Football Federation has announced that it will challenge the verdict, citing irregularities in the proceedings.

results.title: Amnesty calls for ICC genocide probe over Israel's impact on births in Gaza
results.content: Amnesty International on Wednesday urged the International Criminal Court to investigate whether Israeli officials committed genocide in Gaza, citing measures it says have prevented births and severely harmed women's reproductive health. The rights group said it had serious concerns that these effects were intentional, while acknowledging it could not reach a definitive conclusion.
